To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
people use causal models to make sense of what has happened, and to allocate moral and legal responsibility.

(1) people’s causal reasoning is guided by a set of principles that are similar to the principles that govern scientific causal reasoning, (2) people’s causal judgments are sensitive to a variety of factors that are not captured by standard for- and butfor accounts, (3) legal and moral judgments are guided by the same set of principles, and (4) the causal model framework provides a unified and principled account of people’s causal reasoning and its relation to legal and moral reasoning

(a) people’s commonsense notions of causation are rooted in structural models that are based on the counterfactual notion of causation; (b) legal concepts of causion are closely related to commonsense notions of causal reasoning, and are tailored to the concerns of responsibility attribution; and (c) the methods people use to evaluate evidence are also rooted in structural models, and are tailored towards the concerns of evidence evaluation
In summary, our research is concerned with
the causal models people construct, and how they reason about them.
the role of causal reasoning in legal and moral cognition.
how people use causal models to understand and explain events and to make moral judgments, including judgments about responsibility, blame and punishment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence shows that causation is a central concept in everyday reasoning, legal reasoning, and moral reasoning, and that it is best understood in terms of causal models and counterfactors.

the causal model framework is an important tool for understanding the way in which people think about and reason about causation in legal and moral contexts, and that the framework can be used to understand the way in which legal systems and institutions deal with causation.
causal models are critical in legal and moral judgments and reasoning.

the causal model framework is the best available framework for understanding how people reason about causation in everyday contexts, and it is also the best framework for legal reasoning about causation.
